title: Request Chronicle Annotator: SDK extraction, end-to-end span anchors, and safe async propagation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Over the past two quarters we've seen a class of incidents where request ancestry is lost or substantially delayed when requests traverse proxies, websockets, or async worker queues. Root causes include inconsistent header normalization in edge SDKs, late instrumentation attachment in frameworks, and brittle assumptions about a single propagator type.

Goal:
Ship a lightweight cross-language SDK middleware (Request Chronicle Annotator) that: 1) deterministically extracts canonical request metadata at the earliest possible boundary, 2) attaches a compact, immutable request fingerprint and stable span anchor to the request context, and 3) emits a small provenance stamp for downstream services to observe without requiring heavy payload changes. This should reduce lost-context incidents and improve attach-point accuracy for sampled traces.

Design highlights / decisions:
- Extraction layer: single canonical extractor per SDK that understands multiple incoming carriers (http headers, websocket handshake metadata, GRPC metadata, custom edge metadata). The extractor normalizes keys and translates legacy header variants (x-rd-span / rd-span-id / traceparent) into a canonical envelope.
- Request fingerprint: 128-bit compact canonical fingerprint derived from stable fields (incoming trace id if present, request start timestamp truncated to 1s, client-id or ip hash). Fingerprint purpose is to help correlate logs/metrics when span ids are lost; it is NOT meant to replace trace ids.
- Stable span anchor: create an early synthetic span anchor with well-known operation name ("req.anchor.annotator") and attach to context. The anchor is non-sampled by default, purely to provide a consistent parent for subsequent spans when the original parent is missing.
- Provenance stamp: small JSON-ish header (base64 encoded) with schema v1 {fp, extracted_trace_hint, extraction_version}. Size target < 128 bytes. Downstream services can opt-in to copy the stamp to logs or propagate it on async queues.
- Async safety: APIs expose light-weight fence/restore calls for common runtimes (Node async_hooks shim, Go context wrapper, Python contextvars helper). For frameworks where we can't auto-instrument reliably, the SDK exposes a single explicit API (attachChronicle(ctx)) consumers can call in worker entrypoints.
- Sampling and cost controls: Annotator adds a sampling hint header rather than forcing sampling. By default we apply conservative sampling (only annotate 1% of requests for high-volume public endpoints) and expose config via env + Console rollout controls.
- Performance budget: per-request overhead should be < 200ns on hot path for compiled languages and < 1ms for interpreted languages. Microbenchmarks included in PRs.

Alternatives considered:
- Purely rely on existing propagators (W3C Trace-Context) — rejected because legacy clients and edge proxies often rewrite headers unpredictably.
- In-band payload changes (modify request bodies) — rejected due to backwards compatibility and compliance concerns.

Acceptance criteria (what "Done" looks like):
- SDKs (Node + Go) include annotator with normalized extraction and provenance header emitted under feature flag.
- Automated integration test replicates typical header mutation scenarios (edge rewrite, websocket upgrade, queue fanout) and shows <1% lost-context rate compared to current baseline.
- End-to-end microbenchmarks show <1% p50 latency regression and no more than 3% p99 regression in worst-case language SDK.
- Console dashboard: new "Annotator health" panel showing annotated_request_rate, lost_context_rate, provenance_header_size_p95, and anchor_creation_failures; alerted at customer-impacting thresholds.
- PRs: code reviews completed and performance tests in CI passing.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flag on in internal staging with Node + Go SDK (dark traffic on 15% of requests) for 2 weeks. Verify metrics.
2) Expand to 50% and enable provenance header copy in logs for a subset of services.
3) Enable for all traffic, then add Python + Java SDKs next cycle.

Instrumentation & observability checks:
- Add unit tests for header normalization mapping table (include legacy variants).
- Add fuzz tests that mutate headers and ensure canonical envelope stable.
- Add system test that replays production header mutation traces captured during incidents.
- Dashboard queries and dashboards created in the Console project: links below.

comments: 2025-11-03 | Aisha Patel: Initial writeup posted. Key risk is cross-language parity and potential increase in header sizes. Asked for perf target alignment with infra team.
2025-11-05 | Marco Chen: Spike completed for Node. Prototype extractor added as middleware in SDK; microbench shows +0.12ms median, p99 +0.9ms on Node. Will optimize path to reduce allocations.
2025-11-07 | Leah Goldberg (Design): Reviewed header copy UX; recommended default 'do-not-leak' mode for PII-sensitive headers and a Console toggle for operators.
2025-11-09 | SRE: Reviewed failure modes; suggested graceful degradation where annotator returns a no-op when extraction throws; added requirement to never raise unhandled exceptions on hot path.

2025-11-11 | Marco Chen: Updated prototype to use object pooling and preallocated buffers for provenance stamp. Node microbench improved to p99 +0.35ms. Filed PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/compare/feat/chronicle-annotator
2025-11-14 | PM review (Ravi Singh): Asked for a dashboard tile showing 'lost_context_rate' by service and env; added to acceptance criteria and dashboard plan.
2025-11-16 | Security (Anika Rao): Quick review - flagged that provenance stamp should not include raw client IP; we replaced it with a one-way hash and noted in spec. Security review not blocking.

2025-11-18 | Marco Chen: Running staging rollout to 15%. Early metrics: annotated_request_rate 14.7% (target 15%), lost_context_rate down from 0.83% to 0.12% for tested endpoints. No increased error rate observed. Next: ramp and add Go SDK implementation parity work.
Follow-ups: create 'Chronicle cookbook' for integrators, add Python shim ticket, and include a small migration note for customers that copy headers to logs.
notes: Keep the public API minimal: attachChronicle(ctx) & restoreChronicle(ctx). Avoid automatic downstream copying unless opt-in. Monitor provenance_header_size_p95 closely.
